items.title: Jerome Richardson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: They did it to their own feelings and that’s what Duke Ellington’s music was

ctx.x: Yeah. Ellington had a way of making them sound the best that they could.

Well he wrote for them. And you can, well Ellington’s band is a unique band in that they did write for those guys. So consequently, anybody sitting in the band, you could take thirteen pieces or however many that band was, of different guys, playing the same music, won’t sound the same. They will not sound the same. Because they took Duke’s music and bent it to their own feelings. They did it to their own feelings and that’s what Duke Ellington’s music was, what it came out to be. So nobody could come behind that.
Interesting. What brought you back to the West Coast, was it in the late ‘60s?
